notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); the package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware was attached or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], Adroit_hand.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. The card has no entry_symbols, so there was no symbol to verify; the card's first model exists at Adroit_hand.xml:1 and its includes exist. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; each ctrl element is checked by the bridge against the model's actuator_ctrlrange (24 position actuators, resources/joint_position_actuation.xml:14-37) before data.ctrl is written, then mj_step runs ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The world state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed); the fake's model shape is 31 qpos, 30 qvel and 24 ctrl (24 hinge joints plus the ball's free joint). The card's second model, Adroit_hand_withOverlay.xml, is not served: one package serves one model; changing model_path and facts serves the other. No deviation from the card: the family-config decision and the MujocoDriver helper express the model.

WHY THIS SHAPE: the upstream is a set of MJCF models, not a Python SDK, so the family helper is right. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py (the form the SDK's own MujocoDriver tests use). The stand-in parses the same MJCF text and its includes for the joint dimensions, actuator count and control ranges, but integrates a placeholder motion of each actuated hinge toward its control value; it loads no mesh and resolves no contact, equality or tendon constraint. The fidelity gaps list every difference. The sim path (a backend that backends does not name, which imports the real mujoco) was not run.

NOT COVERED: MuJoCo itself was never imported, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine; the model comments out its base free joint (resources/chain.xml:14), so the 4-DOF arm described in README.md:6 is not in this scene and the hand is fixed to the world; the only free body is the ball, whose dynamics the fake does not integrate; the mesh paths in resources/assets.xml:34-44 point at ../Adroit/resources/meshes, which does not resolve inside this clone, so a real engine load was not attempted; the overlay model and the tendon torque actuation variant are not served; there is no rendering; no physical Adroit hand or arm is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware.

WARNINGS (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, the integer/numeric inputs the simulator family derives. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the scene and its includes, per-actuator control-range refusals with zero effect, state following the control target, reset, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. No site-limits.example.json is needed: the control envelope is derived from the model and there is no operator-required bound.
